bug_semantics: Etherpad generated import/export working-file names in the shared process temporary directory from Math.random(), then used ordinary write, rename, and converter operations that follow existing symbolic links. A local low-privilege user who can predict a token and pre-create the corresponding /tmp path as a symlink can redirect Etherpad's file operation to a target writable by the Etherpad process, causing disclosure or overwrite; import output can contain attacker-influenced converted document content.
flaw_origin: The earliest causal origin is eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46: the initial document-export implementation created node/ExportHandler.js with Math.floor(Math.random()*new Date().getTime()), a hard-coded /tmp/eplite_export_ path, fs.writeFile(), and converter output at a sibling predictable path. b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f added the same design to import two days later. Commits 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f and b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b later changed the token formula to Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF, reducing it to the advisory's exact 32-bit form, but they did not originate the insecure shared-temp predictable-name mechanism.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object records author Peter 'Pita' Martischka <petermartischka@googlemail.com> and committer Peter 'Pita' Martischka <petermartischka@googlemail.com>; its message is 'Added support for document export, no link from the pad so far' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot marker/trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/ether/etherpad/security/advisories/GHSA-2jwf-f4xq-f24h identifies <=3.0.0 as affected, >=3.1.0 as patched, and PR https://github.com/ether/etherpad/pull/7784 / commit 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 as the fix. `git log -L '/randNum = Math.floor(Math.random/,+3:node/handler/ExportHandler.js' 1955bdec9a0f0448e5b04638f0e69ed3b9210f39` reaches eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 and shows that commit adding Math.random()*new Date().getTime(), /tmp/eplite_export_, and fs.writeFile; the analogous ImportHandler -L trace reaches b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f. The same traces show e8d84b605809cec49ea08ce02ee83d653369334b only replacing hard-coded /tmp with tempDirectory and 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f / b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b changing the already-insecure formula to 0xFFFFFFFF. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 83829759e9ee59beb28730c761d8d6979a95b359 -- node/ExportHandler.js` returns empty, while `git show eeddf134... -- node/ExportHandler.js` shows the file and vulnerable operations as newly added, directly proving immediate-parent absence. `git show --name-status --find-renames 1239ce7f284821ad4ce51f8219c480ff557a5b86` shows the handlers renamed into src/node/handler, and 331cf3d79fe7c80cb0fb0ed2b1742be521e1344c records R098/R087 JS-to-TypeScript migrations, so neither is an origin. `git merge-base --is-ancestor eeddf134... 1.0` and the same check against v3.0.0 succeed. Tag v3.0.0 resolves to 149c6a24e73761fc06bc9e61b93bc04be6bc044e, where `git grep` finds Math.floor(Math.random() * 0xFFFFFFFF) at ExportHandler.ts:159 and ImportHandler.ts:86. The merge base of fix 8c6104c5... and v3.0.0 is the v3.0.0 commit itself, proving the fix is not in that tag. Tag v3.1.0 resolves to fa1c6b2e43d0510c851643cb7ba67cf042331a37; 8c6104c5... is its ancestor, and `git grep` finds crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') at ExportHandler.ts:164 and ImportHandler.ts:90. `git show 8c6104c5... --` those two handlers directly replaces both vulnerable expressions, so the advisory fix and direct fix are the same commit. `git cat-file commit eeddf134...` supplies the BIC-only authorship/trailer evidence quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins with the July 2011 export feature, not with the 2023/2024 TypeScript copies or the 2026 advisory. eeddf134 first combined a non-cryptographic Math.random-derived token, a shared /tmp namespace, and link-following file/converter operations; its parent lacks the entire handler. Import acquired the same design in b13fbbf. The November 2011 0xFFFFFFFF edits made the current expression but inherited the same security defect, and subsequent directory/TypeScript changes are renames or migrations, so selecting any of them would mistake textual churn for causation. The flaw survived into v3.0.0 and was directly removed by 8c6104c5, which substitutes 128-bit crypto.randomBytes tokens in both handlers and is contained by v3.1.0. The smallest causal BIC is therefore the single-parent, non-squash eeddf134 commit. Its commit object has only the named human author/committer and no AI trailer or bot identity. Under the required BIC-only attribution rule, later AI involvement in discovery or remediation cannot attribute this 2011 introduction, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
